nodes.label: User
nodes.description: You, writing in an Obsidian note (markdown or a canvas node). You type a trigger phrase followed by a question; the plugin takes it from there.

nodes.label: InlinePiSuggest
nodes.description: The markdown trigger provider. When you type ;; in a normal note it wakes, scans the line before the cursor, and catches the question as `query`. It deliberately declines canvas node editors (#18) so it cannot hijack the keystroke there.

nodes.label: InlinePiCanvasSuggest
nodes.description: The canvas twin (added with the #18 fix, Oct 30). Two stacked trigger providers used to both match ;; and the markdown one won on canvas, where Obsidian provides no TFile — so canvas ;; dead-ended. Now this provider only fires inside canvas node editors.

nodes.label: selectSuggestion
nodes.description: Runs when you pick the suggestion from the popup. It holds your question as `value`, inserts the pending callout, captures the note text around the cursor, and passes `value` into the payload build — the question now travels the whole way (#10 closed Oct 28).

nodes.label: insertPendingCallout
nodes.description: Creates the answer box (`> [!claude] {query}`) in the note and stores your question on it as `CalloutInstance.query`. Since T42 the box does NOT stream token-by-token — it holds a static pending header, live progress goes to the status bar, and it is filled in one shot when pi settles.

nodes.label: prepareCanvasCallout
nodes.description: The canvas twin of selectSuggestion: takes the query, creates the callout node in the canvas, saves the canvas file before sending (so the node exists on disk), and passes `query` into the payload build.

nodes.label: buildPromptInstructions
nodes.description: Assembles the message pi receives: the rewritten standing instructions (PREFIX, #12), the note path, a ±50-line window of the note around the cursor (prior callouts stripped, truncated to 8k chars), and — since #10 closed — a `## Question` section. The signature now takes all four: (notePath, cursorLine, noteText, question).

nodes.label: PiClient.prompt
nodes.description: The plugin's messenger to the hidden pi process. A single shared client serves every ;; prompt; requests queue and run one at a time. It also accepts aborts — from the AbortWatcher or the user.

nodes.label: pi process
nodes.description: A separate headless copy of pi running in the background, started the way pi's own RpcClient does it: `node cli.js --mode rpc --no-session --thinking off`. Thinking is off because ;; Q&A is a fast inline exchange — reasoning models otherwise stream long thinking deltas before any text and the box looks frozen. Receives the payload over stdin, streams events back over stdout.

nodes.label: delta / activity / settle
nodes.description: pi's streaming signals, routed by prompt id (stale ids are dropped so a late delta can't corrupt the next run): text deltas, the activity phase (thinking / tool / responding, #6) shown live in the status bar, and the final settlement.

nodes.label: onSettle
nodes.description: When pi finishes, the answer box is replaced wholesale: `> [!claude-done]+ {query}` with the answer under a **Pi:** label (formerly a hardcoded **Claude:** label, #13). Abort and error each get their own callout so the note always tells you how a run ended.

nodes.label: AbortWatcher
nodes.description: The kill switch. While a callout is pending, the watcher checks on every note edit that its header line still exists unchanged. Delete or change the box → the pi run is aborted. The plugin's own writes are suppressed via beginFlush()/endFlush() so filling the answer box never aborts itself.

cards.title: What this is
items: The path a ;; prompt takes through inline-pi, snapshot dated 2026-11-01 at commit 40d21ca.
Two trigger providers (markdown + canvas, the #18 fix) converge on the answer box; the payload build receives the question from both paths (#10 closed 2026-10-28).
The return path routes pi's events to the status bar and fills the callout in one shot on settle (T42).

cards.title: The payload pi receives
items: Rewritten standing instructions, PREFIX (#12): answer from the note in front of you; tools only when the question genuinely needs live data.
The note path plus a ±50-line window around the cursor — prior Q&A callouts stripped so they can't be mimicked, capped at 8k chars.
A ## Question section carrying the actual question — the edge that was missing before #10.

cards.title: Safety valves
items: AbortWatcher kills the run if you delete or edit the pending answer box — the plugin's own writes are exempt (beginFlush/endFlush).
Events are gated by prompt id: a late delta from an already-settled prompt can't corrupt the next one.
Prompts queue and run one at a time on the shared pi process.

cards.title: Keeping this current
items: This is a dated snapshot, not a live view — when the flow changes, regenerate rather than trust this page.
The authoring source (candidate JSON) is committed next to this HTML in docs/diagrams/ — a refresh means updating it and re-running archify finalize.
Rendered with Archify; every node cites the src/ lines it was verified against.
